correctness.rationale: The infinite-past convolution yields conditional Gaussian particles with common random variance V∈(a,b). Stationary phase flux has density g(v)= v/ (vbar Beta(p,q) Δ) ((v-a)/Δ)^(p-1)((b-v)/Δ)^(q-1), where p=r1/(2mu1), q=r2/(2mu2); beta normalization follows exactly. Given V=v, N E_N/v is chi²_N, yielding exact density. Stirling gives sqrt(N)/(2 sqrt(pi) s) exp[-N I(s|v)] uniformly over compact v∈[a,b] for fixed s. Minimizing I produces rates at a,s,b in lower/interior/upper regions. Watson endpoint Laplace gives N^(1/2-p), N^(1/2-q) and Gamma leading factors for fixed exterior s, with one more N^-1 for tail probabilities. Substitutions s=a+z/sqrt(N), v=a+y/sqrt(N) and analogously at b with Gaussian domination give the locally uniform edge profiles and N^((1-p)/2)/N^((1-q)/2) endpoint height laws.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS for sharp out-of-support sample quadratic-energy density asymptotics and two finite-size Gaussian-smoothed energy edges. Biroli–Kulkarni–Majumdar–Schehr 2023/24 establishes the exact latent variance and Gaussian conditional joint law and related extremal/order statistics, which are explicitly credited; Biroli–Larralde–Majumdar–Schehr 2023 gives a generic conditional-iid sum interior limit, also credited. Neither inspected source states the sample-squared-position outside-support polynomial powers/leading constants and Gaussian edge profiles, though these are derivable by additional standard Watson/Laplace analysis; possible prior implicit coverage by broader scale-mixture saddle results remains.
residual_risks: A published general endpoint-Laplace theorem for Gaussian scale mixtures may imply the sharp formulas without presenting this physical observable.
Finite-size edge asymptotics are pointwise fixed parameters, locally uniform for bounded z, not a double-scaling or heat/work result.
